hook: A boy pharaoh who ruled briefly, and whose untouched tomb made him the most famous of them all.

pages.x: Tutankhamun was the son of Akhenaten, the pharaoh who banned the old gods and worshipped only the sun disc. He became king at about nine, named Tutankhaten. His advisers soon turned back the clock: the old gods returned, the court left Akhenaten's new city of Amarna, and the boy became Tutankhamun, "living image of Amun".

He died at about nineteen, around 1323 BC. Scans of his mummy show a broken leg, a club foot and malaria, but no one knows for sure what killed him. He died so suddenly that he was buried in a small tomb that may have been meant for someone else.

On 4 November 1922, Howard Carter, paid by Lord Carnarvon, found steps leading down to a sealed tomb. Peering in by candlelight, Carter was asked if he could see anything. "Yes," he said, "wonderful things." It was the only royal tomb in the valley found almost untouched, with over 5,000 objects.

Over the face of the mummy lay a mask of solid gold weighing more than ten kilograms, inlaid with blue lapis lazuli, quartz and coloured glass. It shows the young king as the god Osiris. It is perhaps the most famous object from the whole ancient world.

A few months after the tomb was opened, Lord Carnarvon died from an infected mosquito bite. Newspapers spread the tale of a "curse of the pharaohs" that killed anyone who disturbed the king. Howard Carter, who spent ten years working in the tomb, lived until 1939.

Tutankhamun was a minor king who reigned for only ten years. His fame comes from death: his nearly untouched tomb showed the world the full splendour of a pharaoh's burial and set off a worldwide craze for ancient Egypt.
pts: Brought back Egypt's old gods after his father
His tomb was found almost intact in 1922
His golden mask became the icon of ancient Egypt
